answer: Neighborhood terrace scoring. Each new agent is placed on a public adjacency terrace with a bounded number of peers, and its routing weight depends on how many distinct existing neighborhoods it can transact across. To fabricate a sybil that reaches useful reach, an attacker must buy real positions in many separate clusters—not just many keys—because a gale of fresh identities clustered together collapses into one weakly connected grove and earns near-zero reach. Cost: distinct neighborhood entry per identity, scaling linearly with target reach.
